evidence.note: R-path-merge is CONFIRMED (already filed): baselines are gate process union 992 h / 1,322 items (~0.75 h/item), cycle p50 1.33 h p90 9.7 h, process share 27%%, sequential review-pair share 55%%, superseded passes 119 h, parked 22%%; keyed by env fingerprint. Claim probed over the frozen twelve-item log: effect() computes all six metrics from the existing facts fold (no second collector) and delta = current - baseline. Falsifier: a metric needing a second collector, or an unknown env key not falling back to canonical.

Applied: r-reuse-core (reuses metrics.paths process union + summary.completed_spans, no second collector), r-small-files (one module + test), r-everything-configurable (BASELINES table overridable, PARKED_THRESHOLD_S constant), r-no-shell (pure data + text), r-tell-dont-discover (next call names ddflow perf report), r-unavailable (below floor is None with n, never zero). Decisions: D-path-merge-answers (a merged gate keeps its own outcome), D-lock-lifecycle-answers, D-perf-metrics-answers (env-keyed comparisons always present).

ddflow/services/perf/path_effect.py (a pure fold over facts.collect): baseline() (R-path-merge keyed by env fingerprint), current() (six metrics), effect() (before/after with delta), text() block, plus tests/test_path_effect.py (10 tests). Reuses services.metrics.paths for burst-corrected process union and metrics.summary.completed_spans; no new collector. A figure under [metrics].min_samples is None with its n, never zero.

chunk_findings.detail: Given five completed spans and `min_samples` of 5, but only one span with `cycle_s` set (the other four `None`), `current` still calls `percentile` on that one-element `cycles` list and passes `n=len(spans)` into `_figure`. The floor sees 5 samples, so claim-to-merge p50 and p90 are published instead of `None`, and the reported `n` is completed items rather than cycle observations. The same `n` lets `process_share` pass the floor when `cycle` is the sum of fewer timed spans than `min_samples`, so the ratio is not the sample the floor claims to guard.
chunk_findings.title: current

chunk_findings.detail: A passed verdict with `tree_sha` set, `elapsed_s is None`, and a later outcome on the same item with a different `tree_sha` hits `if o.kind != "passed" or not o.tree_sha or o.elapsed_s is None: continue`, so it adds neither seconds nor `count`. With no other superseded passes and at least one completed span, the figure is `{"value": 0.0, "n": 0}` — the same “true zero” used for a window with no superseded pass — even though a superseded pass occurred and the function’s own contract says an untimed pass adds a count and no seconds.
chunk_findings.title: superseded_pass_hours

chunk_findings.detail: `superseded_pass_s` is an absolute sum over whatever window `ctx` holds, while the only baseline is the full R-path-merge corpus total (`119 * HOUR` over 2026-10-03..11-02). `effect` then does `delta = current - baseline`. A one-day log with 1 superseded hour therefore renders as about ▼118h versus baseline, and a longer post-change log whose hourly rate is better than the baseline still flips to ▲ once the raw sum passes 119 h. The other six figures are rates or percentiles; this one is not normalized, so the before/after arrow is wrong for any window that is not that exact corpus.
chunk_findings.title: superseded_pass_hours / effect

chunk_findings.detail: Claim-to-merge p50/p90 are taken from `cycles = [s.cycle_s for s in spans if s.cycle_s is not None]`, but `_figure` is given `n = len(spans)`, not `len(cycles)`. With `min_samples` 5, five completed spans and only two non-null `cycle_s` values, `n >= minimum` so a percentile of two samples is emitted as a real p50/p90. The sample floor does not apply to the distribution actually summarized.
chunk_findings.title: current

chunk_findings.detail: The function states that a passed verdict with no `elapsed_s` still increments the count and adds no seconds. The guard `o.kind != "passed" or not o.tree_sha or o.elapsed_s is None` drops those rows before `count += 1`. One later different `tree_sha` after an untimed pass therefore returns `{"value": 0.0, "n": 0}` (when any item completed) instead of `n` at least 1, so the data block under-counts superseded passes.
chunk_findings.title: superseded_pass_hours

chunk_findings.detail: `current()` mixes custom dictionary keys (`"superseded_passes"`) into the return value of `_figure()`, which returns a standard metric dictionary containing only `"value"` and `"n"`. Downstream consumers that expect standard figure dicts or unpack keys from `_figure()` will encounter an unexpected `"superseded_passes"` key or missing expected structure when processing `"superseded_pass_s"`. Given a context where `current()` is evaluated, `superseded_pass_s` returns `{"value": ..., "n": ..., "superseded_passes": ...}`, violating the structural contract established by the other metrics.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/path_effect.py:199

chunk_findings.detail: `superseded_pass_hours` sums `elapsed_s` over every item in `ctx.facts.outcomes`, but `current` divides that total by `n_items` from `completed_spans` only and publishes it as superseded-pass hours per merged item. A superseded pass on an item that is not a completed span is still added to `seconds` (and `count`), then attributed to the completed population. Given item A completed with no superseded pass and item B incomplete with a later different `tree_sha` and `elapsed_s=3600`, `n_items` is 1 and `sup_value` is 3600, so the report shows 3600s per merged item even though the merged item contributed 0.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/path_effect.py:current
